newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND TO BOOST FOOD MARKET PROTECTION FROM JULY 1.
newsitem.headline: POLAND TO BOOST FOOD MARKET PROTECTION FROM JULY 1.

text.p: Poland from July 1 will base the duty charged on many food imports on prices estimated by the government and not on their value stated on import documents, PAP news agency reported a senior official as saying on Friday.

"From July, the duty will be levied according to a price set by us on the basis of prices in Europe and not on the basis of value stated in invoices," PAP quoted deputy agriculture minister Jerzy Pilarczyk as saying.
Pilarczyk was quoted as telling reporters in the western city of Opole that the so-called "entry prices" would embrace imports of grains, grain products, meat, sugar, some vegetables and fruits.

The new procedure of calculating imports duty, compatible with regulations of the World Trade Organisation (WTO), will protect domestic food producers against unfair competition, PAP quoted Pilarczyk as saying.
He said that in many cases importers stated false, lower value of products so as to pay lower duty.
No agriculture ministry officials were immediately available to give more details.
